A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ROUTE research. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.13 are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Text-to-SQL evaluations, component ablations, transferability studies, and appendix experiments, including Dr.Spider robustness results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and supplies an additional baseline result in Table 1.

M1.justification: The MSFT objective, noise filtering, and MCP schema-linking, noise-correction, and continuation-writing procedures remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1. Section 3 only adjusts the wording of ROUTE's name.

E1.justification: Both versions retain SPIDER and BIRD training and evaluation, the three SPIDER variants, and Dr.Spider perturbation evaluations in Appendix A.5. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds reported participation of Qwen2.5-7B + SFT in the SPIDER test-set comparison through a Test-EX score of 82.8; v1 leaves this cell blank. This baseline already appears in development-set comparisons, and the other comparator memberships remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, model configurations, EX/TS/VES metrics, training budgets, and inference settings remain unchanged. Filling the Table 1 result cell does not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: The component ablations, schema-linking analyses, transferability and upper-bound studies, Dr.Spider robustness tests, and qualitative noisy-pair examples are unchanged. Moving Figure 4 introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Statistical and uncertainty reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 fills the previously blank SPIDER Test-EX entry for Qwen2.5-7B + SFT with 82.8. All other numerical results and qualitative findings, including the appendix results and relocated Figure 4, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The task definitions, training objective in Equation 1, schema-merging expression in Equation 2, and other mathematical formulations are unchanged. No theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning multitask training, collaborative prompting, transferability, and narrowing the performance gap with closed-source LLMs.

C2.justification: Interpretations of task complementarity, schema linking, transferability, and upper-bound performance remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning inference costs and the remaining performance gap.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware, training-data counts, filtering details, Algorithm 1, and prompt templates are unchanged. The code/data hyperlink has the same destination, and Appendix A.13 retains the same reproducibility statement.

R1.justification: The cited works, Section 2 related-work discussion, and Appendix A.8 comparisons with earlier methods are unchanged. The conference publication header does not revise the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 updates the publication header, adds the Tianfu Jincheng Laboratory affiliation and funding acknowledgments, and makes small wording changes in the abstract and Section 3. The scientific narrative and appendix structure remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 4 moves from page 10 to page 9 and is reduced in size without changing its plotted content. The upper-bound discussion, Tables 6–7, and following sections are repositioned to accommodate the acknowledgments.

improvement.justification: Filling the missing Qwen2.5-7B + SFT test score in Table 1 makes the baseline comparison more complete, and the acknowledgments add funding disclosure. These are limited reporting improvements; the method, substantive analyses, appendices, and scientific conclusions remain unchanged.
